answer: Each epoch the protocol posts M, unused mine-rights still held by established keys this window. A first-seen submit must attach k unique mine-waivers from unrelated established keys that still had unused mine-rights, k=1 plus first-seen already included. One joiner needs 1; the tenth needs 10, so the next head costs more (triangle n(n+1)/2). A waiver is a thread: that key cannot attest for the rest of the window, lend the slot, or reset M. At the nadir of leftover mine-rights the river of honest attestors dries. Refuse the waivers and the submit is dropped.
